item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows a $4$-by-$4$ grid coloured in checkerboard black and white. Nitya removes the two opposite white corner squares marked in the figure. She wants to cover the remaining region with $2 \times 1$ tiles that do not overlap and leave no gaps.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: The answer is the word checkerboard, because that colouring word is printed with the grid.
options.B: Yes: the remaining region has $14$ squares, an even count, so $2 \times 1$ tiles can cover it.
options.C: No: each $2 \times 1$ tile covers one black and one white square, but the remaining region has unequal black and white counts.
options.D: The same colouring argument also settles tiling of every even-area shape, including shapes with no grid colouring.
